# #8690 PERMANENT-EXCLUSION REGISTER — the classification of every line still in
# compact_block_divergences_2419.txt.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The inventory counts sites that DIVERGE. It says nothing
# about whether a site MAY be normalized, and by the end of the sweep those are
# almost disjoint questions: 47 lines remain and ~43 of them must never be
# normalized. A bare count of 47 reads as 47 units of work, and the only way to
# "finish" it is to normalize sites the guards exist to protect. This file is
# what the inventory's remainder actually means.
#
# FORMAT: <site>\t<class>\t<reason>
#
# CLASSES
#   partial          something already consumes part of the tail. Truncating it
#                    removes a value that is READ, on a config that commits
#                    clean. Forbidden to every scope by
#                    TestNormalizerScopeNeverCoversAPartialSite8690.
#   gate-open-question
#                    the disarm arm reds here: rejected at strict commit with the
#                    pass disabled, accepted with it enabled. THAT IS A QUESTION,
#                    NOT A VERDICT, and this register got it wrong at first by
#                    recording such reds as permanent.
#                    The arm cannot distinguish a gate refusing the packed
#                    SPELLING (harmful to disarm) from one refusing the
#                    CONSEQUENCE OF THE DROP — where the pass repairs the drop
#                    and the acceptance is correct. Only a person can, and the
#                    verdict's home is the `benign` map in
#                    compact_normalize_scope_8690_test.go.
#                    PROOF THAT THIS DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING: `security ipsec
#                    policy <p> proposal-set` and its ike collateral were listed
#                    here as permanent on this arm's red alone. Classified, they
#                    were BENIGN — the gate refuses the dropped proposal-set and
#                    says so in its own message — and they normalized in
#                    0c4818aa0. Two of the entries this register called permanent
#                    were available work.
#                    So these are NOT permanent. They are unanswered questions,
#                    and answering one is the available work.
#   gate-confirmed   classified BY A PERSON as a genuine disarm, with the
#                    evidence. Permanent. Currently empty: no site here has been
#                    carried through step 3.
#   gate-collateral  not itself gate-disarming, but shares a (container, head)
#                    pair with a `gate` site, and the predicate's two arguments
#                    cannot express the difference. Lost with the pair.
#   unmeasurable     the census fixture cannot produce a type-valid value, so
#                    gate status cannot be measured. NOT known-safe.
#   unreachable      no (container, head) rule can express it — the container is
#                    wildcard-named, so production passes an arbitrary instance
#                    name where a rule would need a keyword.
#   hazard           normalizing breaks documented, shipped behaviour that no
#                    disarm measurement detects.
#   open             genuinely available work with no gate in the way.
#   wrong-remedy     normalizing this site does NOT fix its defect, and admitting
#                    it would remove inventory lines while the reachable harm is
#                    untouched. Permanent for the count, but for a reason unlike
#                    the others: not forbidden, not a no-op — a FALSE FIX. The
#                    entry must name the real defect and the cell that shows the
#                    remedy missing its target.
#   owed-own-change  the fix is correct but the VEHICLE is not a family sweep: it
#                    changes behaviour that owes its own change and a smoke.
#                    Distinct from `open` because sweeping it would be wrong even
#                    though normalizing it is right.
#   no-drop-measured MEASURED, at every reachable spelling, to drop nothing. The
#                    pass is not load-bearing here in either direction, so there
#                    is no fix to make and no behaviour to change. Distinct from
#                    `unmeasurable`, whose reason is a fixture limitation that
#                    evaporates the moment someone improves the fixture; this
#                    reason does not. Evidence is executable, not prose:
#                    compact_scheduler_name_measured_8690_test.go.
#
#                    THIS CLASS REPLACED `owed-own-change`, WHICH EXISTED FOR
#                    ONE HOUR AND HELD ONLY THESE TWO SITES. That class was
#                    created to hold an argument I reasoned out and did not run:
#                    that a packed `scheduler-name` is silently dropped, leaving
#                    a PERMANENTLY-ACTIVE security policy, so normalizing it was
#                    a correct fix owing a failover smoke. Measured, every clause
#                    is false. The argument was built on a spelling nobody
#                    writes: I reasoned about a hierarchical brace-elided form
#                    instead of running the flat `set` form operators actually
#                    use. A measurement of the wrong spelling is not a weaker
#                    measurement, it is a measurement of a different question.
#   unclassified     in another lane's family and NOT measured here. Deliberately
#                    distinct from `open`: "nobody has checked" is a third state,
#                    and recording it as available asserts a measurement that was
#                    not taken.
#
# THIS REGISTER WAS WRONG TWICE IN ITS FIRST HOUR, BOTH TIMES IN THE
# OVER-RESTRICTIVE DIRECTION, AND BOTH ERRORS HAD THE SAME SHAPE: a result
# established at one granularity, recorded at a finer one.
#
#   `security ipsec policy <p> proposal-set` (+ its ike collateral) were listed
#   permanent on the DISARM ARM'S RED. That red is a question, not a verdict —
#   the arm cannot tell a gate refusing the packed spelling from one refusing
#   the CONSEQUENCE of the drop. Classified by a person, they were BENIGN, and
#   they normalized in 0c4818aa0.
#
#   `chassis device-map interface` / `unmapped-interface-policy` were listed
#   `hazard` on a PER-FAMILY bisection: admitting every chassis pair reds three
#   redundancy-group cells. True of the family; not true of these two sites,
#   whose pairs are different. Measured per site they are safe, and they
#   normalized alongside schedulers.
#
# Four sites this file called permanent were available work. The lesson is the
# one the sweep has been applying everywhere else and this register did not:
# CHECK PER SITE, NOT PER FAMILY — and treat an instrument's red as the
# question it is until a person answers it.
#
# SITES ARRIVE AS WELL AS LEAVE, and the register has to carry both. Twelve
# entered between the #8729 measurement and this file landing — ten `services
# rpm probe` leaves and two `policies ... scheduler-name` — not because a
# compact-blind reader was introduced, but because another lane's
# value-synthesis work made them OBSERVABLE to the census. `schedulers scheduler
# <s> {start,stop}-date` arrived the same way mid-flight and moved a measured
# family from 21 sites to 23.
#
# A blind-spot count that RISES is the instrument improving, and the register
# must not treat an arrival as a defect. What it must do is refuse to let one
# pass unclassified, which is what the set-equality assertion does.
#
# EVERY MEASUREMENT NAMES THE COMMIT IT WAS TAKEN AT, and that is not
# bookkeeping. Two classifications in this register described sites that had
# already left the inventory by the time anyone read them — a reader checking
# the file finds nothing and cannot tell whether the site was fixed or was never
# there. A verdict about a live artefact is only meaningful with its `as-of`.
#
# AND EVERY VERDICT HERE IS CONDITIONAL ON THE SCOPE AT THAT COMMIT. A
# `gate-confirmed` or benign classification says what WOULD happen if the pair
# were admitted; none of these pairs is admitted today, so nothing in this file
# describes a live defect. Writing "is a disarm" where the evidence says "would
# be a disarm if admitted" is the difference between a hole in the tree and a
# hole caught before it was opened — this register only ever records the second.
#
# THIS FILE IS A GATE, NOT A REGISTRY. The guard asserts set-equality with the
# inventory in BOTH directions, and drives every non-`open` site through the
# real normalizer to confirm the pass still leaves it alone. A listed site that
# becomes admissible reds; an inventory site missing from this file reds. An
# exclusion list that only accumulates is a place to hide defects.

security policies from-zone xpfarg xpfarg xpfarg policy xpfarg scheduler-name	wrong-remedy	THE NORMALIZER DOES NOT FIX THIS SITE, and admitting it would clear the evidence without fixing the defect. Cite: scheduler_name_forwarding_8690_test.go (runnable). THE HARM IS REAL, AND ITS SOURCE IS A CONFIG FILE, NOT THE CLI: flat `set … policy p1 match …` then `set … policy p1 scheduler-name S` MERGES into one policy carrying both (measured, both orderings, both compile paths). The duplicate shape arrives as a FILE with the two statements as siblings — hand-edited, written by an older build, or pushed by an un-upgraded primary — which is exactly the population Store.Load and Store.SyncApply exist to accept. On the LENIENT path — production's Load and SyncApply (configstore/store.go: boot config load and HA config sync) — that compiles to TWO policies named p1: the operator's (src=[any], PERMIT) with sched="", and a spurious match-less DENY. A policy written TIME-LIMITED runs PERMANENTLY ACTIVE. BUT NORMALIZING PUTS THE SCHEDULE ON THE WRONG ONE: measured with the pair ADMITTED (load-bearing — at master, with the pair excluded, the duplicate carries sched="" under both skipNorm settings, since the pass touches 0 nodes and both runs are identical), the pass moves the packed tail into the DUPLICATE's body — operator's policy still sched="", duplicate gets "S". The defect is that the second `policy p1 …` statement DUPLICATES rather than merging (#3473; lane-8526's #8436 duplicate-block work), which is a policy-level defect, not a brace-elision one. Admitting the pair changes only the census's inert spelling, where the policy has no body and does nothing either way — so it removes two inventory lines and looks like progress while the harm is untouched. WHY TWO EARLIER MEASUREMENTS DISAGREED, recorded so this is not re-derived a fourth time: the STRICT path REJECTS the elided spelling, so cfg is nil and there is nothing to inspect — a gate firing is the ABSENCE of a compiled result, not evidence about one; and any skipNorm comparison taken while the pair is EXCLUDED is vacuous, because the pass touches 0 nodes and both sides are the same run
security policies global policy xpfarg scheduler-name	wrong-remedy	THE NORMALIZER DOES NOT FIX THIS SITE, and admitting it would clear the evidence without fixing the defect. Cite: scheduler_name_forwarding_8690_test.go (runnable). THE HARM IS REAL, AND ITS SOURCE IS A CONFIG FILE, NOT THE CLI: flat `set … policy p1 match …` then `set … policy p1 scheduler-name S` MERGES into one policy carrying both (measured, both orderings, both compile paths). The duplicate shape arrives as a FILE with the two statements as siblings — hand-edited, written by an older build, or pushed by an un-upgraded primary — which is exactly the population Store.Load and Store.SyncApply exist to accept. On the LENIENT path — production's Load and SyncApply (configstore/store.go: boot config load and HA config sync) — that compiles to TWO policies named p1: the operator's (src=[any], PERMIT) with sched="", and a spurious match-less DENY. A policy written TIME-LIMITED runs PERMANENTLY ACTIVE. BUT NORMALIZING PUTS THE SCHEDULE ON THE WRONG ONE: measured with the pair ADMITTED (load-bearing — at master, with the pair excluded, the duplicate carries sched="" under both skipNorm settings, since the pass touches 0 nodes and both runs are identical), the pass moves the packed tail into the DUPLICATE's body — operator's policy still sched="", duplicate gets "S". The defect is that the second `policy p1 …` statement DUPLICATES rather than merging (#3473; lane-8526's #8436 duplicate-block work), which is a policy-level defect, not a brace-elision one. Admitting the pair changes only the census's inert spelling, where the policy has no body and does nothing either way — so it removes two inventory lines and looks like progress while the harm is untouched. WHY TWO EARLIER MEASUREMENTS DISAGREED, recorded so this is not re-derived a fourth time: the STRICT path REJECTS the elided spelling, so cfg is nil and there is nothing to inspect — a gate firing is the ABSENCE of a compiled result, not evidence about one; and any skipNorm comparison taken while the pair is EXCLUDED is vacuous, because the pass touches 0 nodes and both sides are the same run
services rpm probe xpfarg test xpfarg destination-interface	unclassified	UNKNOWN, and specifically NOT cleared. Admitting it produces no disarm from arm 2 — but it also moves the site into the set arm 2 CANNOT EXAMINE (its reference spelling does not compile in isolation), which reds lane-8388's equality assertion. So arm 2's silence here is the ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, not evidence of absence, and reading it as a pass is the exact mistake this register exists to stop. Entered the inventory after the #8729 measurement from another lane's value-synthesis work, the same way `schedulers scheduler <s> {start,stop}-date` appeared mid-flight.
